evidence: Workbook #20 + quality-checks.md:88 require: committed static baseline; seeding identical every run; no random ids, wall-clock-derived values or boot-time fetch that could move a graded figure; fixed clock the only time source for graded rules. (1) Committed/static: solution is plain source files (package.json, server.js, src/{bootstrap,db,index}.js, src/seed_data.json, public/*). No node_modules, no shipped .db, no build/generation step. task/solution/solve.sh only checks for an open database, then runs `cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/` and `rm -f -- "$database_path" ...`. It does no npm install and no download. It extends the template solve.sh (`cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/`) without changing that contract. task/solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (cmp OK; sha256 a1c65c80...7740 matches the raw-evidence-index entry). git ls-files confirms that the project's src/seed_data.json is tracked. (2) Deterministic seed: db.js:10 reads seed_data.json relative to __dirname. seedIfEmpty (db.js:61-86) inserts users, jobs and applications with ids from the file. Application created_at is the fixed literal '2026-06-15T09:00:00Z' (db.js:75). Messages and notes take created_at from the seed (db.js:79,84). Read markers come from deterministic autoincrement ids (db.js:82-83). The password is the constant from the brief. It reseeds only when users is empty (db.js:62). Measured: I ran db.js open() through a node:sqlite shim that stands in for better-sqlite3 (scratchpad only). Two fresh databases gave an identical full-table dump sha256 fe0bcaf0...f1f7 (users 10, jobs 3, applications 16, messages 127, reads 6, notes 3). Reopening the first database gave the same hash, so there was no reseed. The hash-verified scripted golden run (qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/results/workspace.json) also records 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding'. (3) Randomness and wall clock: crypto.randomBytes appears only in session tokens (index.js:88) and in ids for runtime-created jobs and applications (index.js:60,208,226). new Date() (index.js:59) only stamps runtime-created sessions, activity, actions, notes and messages. Nothing orders or grades by those values. Activity, messages and actions are ordered by autoincrement id (index.js:132-166,189). Board order is the stored position. Candidate application order is `ORDER BY created_at, id` (index.js:173); that order is not graded (rules section 7 and hro_candidate_view grade content, not order). The public brief and rules contain no time-based rule (no deadlines, aging or relative dates). The 15-second live-update window is a judge observation bound, not an app clock rule. No criterion in tests/gates/* or tests/scored/*/judge.toml pins a timestamp or generated id. The only frontend time use is a UTC-pinned display formatter (public/js/app.js:21 timeZone 'UTC'). (4) No boot fetch: the server has no outbound requests. The only fetch( call is the frontend's same-origin API helper (app.js:29). index.html loads only local /styles.css and /js/*.js, and styles.css has no @import or url(). Adversarial probes: (a) An app that seeds with random ids or wall-clock data could still pass the judge if no pinned figure moves. That concerns the submission, not the reference, so it creates no defect for this row. (b) A conforming alternative that uses UUIDs or the real clock for new records cannot fail, because no criterion pins those values. All six raw-evidence artifacts and every matching_source_files hash match the current frozen bytes. Limitation: the seed-repeat check used a node:sqlite shim, not real better-sqlite3 in the agent image. Because seeding performs only plain INSERTs with fixed values, this does not affect the conclusion. No configured judge, Oracle or model score is claimed.
